text.p: Salomon Brothers said in a report it had downgraded Brazilian power utility Celesc to hold from buy.
-- "Despite continued price increases over the past year, Celesc shares continue to trade at a discount to other Brazilian electrical utilities," it said.
-- "However, we believe the market will require the company to have a clearer commitment to efficiency before increasing the stock's valuation to match its peers," it added.
-- It also said its primary investment concern about the company is the firm's majority shareholder, Santa Catarina state government, and its close operating relationship with Celesc.

-- Salomon Brothers noted, however, it is optimistic about market prospects for Celesc "as the company's demand growth should outpace overall demand within Brazilian electrical sector for the next several years."
-- Celesc, formally known as Centrais Eletricas de Santa Catarina, preferred was flat at 1.24 reais earlier on the Sao Paulo bolsa.
